IntegratedLearner

Nalin Arora, Anupreet Porwal and Himel Mallick

2026-03-10

Source: vignettes/IntegratedLearner.Rmd
IntegratedLearner.Rmd

Introduction

This vignette is a practical tutorial for binary, multiclass, continuous, and survival outcome workflows in IntegratedLearner.

The examples use seven small MAE RDS files in inst/extdata, accessed directly with readRDS(system.file("extdata", filename, package = "IntegratedLearner")). Each assay retains at most 25 variable features selected from training data in original order; validation uses identical feature IDs. All original samples and outcomes are kept. These subsets demonstrate the API; they are not intended to reproduce full-cohort scientific results.

IntegratedLearner is designed for multi-omics studies where each assay layer can carry complementary signal and where users want a unified interface for standard integrated learning or standalone cooperative multiview learning. This makes the package a natural fit for Bioconductor workflows built around MultiAssayExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, and curated assay containers.

Within the Bioconductor ecosystem, the package is intended to sit after assay assembly and harmonization, and before downstream interpretation. IntegratedLearner focuses on supervised multi-omics prediction/integration rather than general container management or unsupervised integration.

How this fits in a Bioconductor workflow

In a standard Bioconductor analysis, you would typically import or construct assay-level data, store those assays in a MultiAssayExperiment, inspect the object with standard accessors, fit IntegratedLearner(), and then carry predictions, layer weights, and feature-level summaries into downstream interpretation or visualization steps.

Workflow at a Glance

A compact workflow is:

  1. Construct aligned assays in MultiAssayExperiment.
  2. Inspect experiments and metadata with experiments(), assay(), colData(), and sampleMap().
  3. Fit single-layer and fused predictive models with IntegratedLearner().
  4. Feed predictions, layer weights, and feature summaries into downstream Bioconductor interpretation workflows.

Compared with packages that primarily focus on assay containers, preprocessing, or narrower outcome families, IntegratedLearner is centered on the modeling layer itself: it provides a common interface for continuous, binary, multiclass, and survival prediction while remaining compatible with standard Bioconductor data structures. In that sense, it is intended to complement upstream Bioconductor tools rather than replace them.

The goal is to show a complete end-to-end pattern you can adapt to your own multi-omics study:

  1. Build correctly formatted training/validation inputs.
  2. Fit per-layer, stacked, and concatenated learners.
  3. Interpret model outputs (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy, R2, survival discrimination curves, layer weights, and feature signals).

IntegratedLearner supports two execution modes:

  • Standard IL mode: per-layer base learners, early fusion from concatenated features, and late fusion through a meta-learner.
  • Intermediate/cooperative mode: standalone multiview cooperative learning over feature matrices from each layer.

Cooperative learning is enabled with run_intermediate = TRUE. In this mode, IntegratedLearner skips base learners, early fusion, late fusion, and supervised screening. It is currently supported for continuous, binary, and survival outcomes. For multiclass outcomes, IntegratedLearner prints a message and ignores run_intermediate.

Optional feature selection workflow used in this vignette:

  1. Filtering first (filter_method, filter_pct) on training features.
  2. Screening second (run_screening = TRUE, screen_pct) in a fold-safe manner:
    • selected on fold-training only,
    • applied to fold-validation,
    • repeated for each fold,
    • repeated once on full training data for final model fit.

Installation

Install the release version from Bioconductor with:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("IntegratedLearner")

For the development version, use:

BiocManager::install("himelmallick/IntegratedLearner")

Load Packages 

# Main package
library(IntegratedLearner)

# Tutorial dependencies
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(SuperLearner)
library(caret)
library(cowplot)
library(bayesplot)
library(S4Vectors)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(survival)
if (requireNamespace("multiview", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(multiview)
}
if (use_sl_bart) {
  library(bartMachine)
}

Input Data Contract

This vignette uses MultiAssayExperiment throughout and treats MAE as the primary user-facing entry point. The older PCL input mode is still supported for backward compatibility, but the recommended workflow is to stay inside standard Bioconductor containers for data inspection and model handoff.

For IntegratedLearner, each MAE example should satisfy:

  • each omics layer is stored as a separate experiment, typically a SummarizedExperiment
  • samples are aligned across experiments through MAE colData
  • the outcome column lives in top-level colData
  • the subject identifier column also lives in top-level colData

For survival workflows, colData should contain time and event columns (with event coded as 0/1). You can also keep a convenience survival column such as Y or outcome_surv as a Surv(time, event) object.

You can keep your own column names and map them in the wrapper:

fit <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  outcome_col = "disease_status",
  subject_id_col = "participant_id",
  family = stats::binomial()
)

Automatic coercion in the wrapper:

  • family = gaussian(): outcome is coerced to numeric (errors if conversion fails).
  • binary family = binomial(): two classes are mapped internally to {0,1}.
  • multiclass family = binomial(): class labels are retained.

Standard Bioconductor Accessors

IntegratedLearner is intended to plug into a standard Bioconductor workflow, not replace one. In practice, users should continue to inspect and manipulate their inputs with the usual MultiAssayExperiment and SummarizedExperiment accessors before modeling:

PRISM_MAE <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "PRISM_MAE.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))

mae_example <- PRISM_MAE

# Top-level sample annotations used by IntegratedLearner
head(as.data.frame(S4Vectors::DataFrame(MultiAssayExperiment::colData(mae_example)))[, 1:4])
#>        Diagnosis dysbiosis_score Y subjectID
#> G35127        CD       0.9341207 1    G35127
#> G35128        CD       0.5962602 1    G35128
#> G35152        CD       0.9505732 1    G35152
#> G36347        CD       0.9966957 1    G36347
#> G36348        CD       0.8475403 1    G36348
#> G36349        CD       0.9569372 1    G36349

# Available experiments/layers in the MAE
names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_example))
#> [1] "species"     "metabolites"

# Pull one layer as a SummarizedExperiment
se_example <- MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_example)[[1]]
class(se_example)
#> [1] "SummarizedExperiment"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "SummarizedExperiment"

# Standard assay extraction from the layer
assay_names <- SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se_example)
assay_names
#> [1] "abundance"
head(SummarizedExperiment::assay(se_example, assay_names[1]))

# MAE sample-to-assay mapping
head(MultiAssayExperiment::sampleMap(mae_example))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 3 columns
#>      assay     primary     colname
#>   <factor> <character> <character>
#> 1  species      G35127      G35127
#> 2  species      G35128      G35128
#> 3  species      G35152      G35152
#> 4  species      G36347      G36347
#> 5  species      G36348      G36348
#> 6  species      G36349      G36349

This is the expected Bioconductor pipeline pattern:

  1. Build assay-level objects as SummarizedExperiment instances.
  2. Combine them into a MultiAssayExperiment.
  3. Store outcome and subject identifiers in top-level colData.
  4. Pass the MAE into IntegratedLearner() for layer-wise, early-fusion, and late-fusion modeling.

Minimal MAE Workflow Example

The shortest end-to-end pattern starts from packaged MAE data, uses standard Bioconductor accessors for inspection, and then fits IntegratedLearner().

PRISM_MAE <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "PRISM_MAE.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))

mae_min <- PRISM_MAE

names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_min))
#> [1] "species"     "metabolites"
head(as.data.frame(S4Vectors::DataFrame(MultiAssayExperiment::colData(mae_min)))[, 1:4])
#>        Diagnosis dysbiosis_score Y subjectID
#> G35127        CD       0.9341207 1    G35127
#> G35128        CD       0.5962602 1    G35128
#> G35152        CD       0.9505732 1    G35152
#> G36347        CD       0.9966957 1    G36347
#> G36348        CD       0.8475403 1    G36348
#> G36349        CD       0.9569372 1    G36349
head(MultiAssayExperiment::sampleMap(mae_min))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 3 columns
#>      assay     primary     colname
#>   <factor> <character> <character>
#> 1  species      G35127      G35127
#> 2  species      G35128      G35128
#> 3  species      G35152      G35152
#> 4  species      G36347      G36347
#> 5  species      G36348      G36348
#> 6  species      G36349      G36349

se_min <- MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_min)[[1]]
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se_min)
#> [1] "abundance"
dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(se_min, SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se_min)[1]))
#> [1]  25 155

fit_min <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_min,
  experiment = names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_min))[1:2],
  assay.type = rep("abundance", 2),
  folds = 2,
  base_learner = "SL.mean",
  run_stacked = FALSE,
  run_concat = FALSE,
  print_learner = FALSE,
  family = stats::binomial()
)

names(fit_min)
#>  [1] "model_fits"                         "SL_fits"                           
#>  [3] "X_train_layers"                     "Y_train"                           
#>  [5] "yhat.train"                         "base_learner"                      
#>  [7] "meta_learner"                       "base_screener"                     
#>  [9] "base_screener_used"                 "screening_used"                    
#> [11] "run_concat"                         "run_stacked"                       
#> [13] "run_intermediate"                   "cooperative_rho_grid"              
#> [15] "cooperative_s"                      "drop_poor_performing_layers"       
#> [17] "fusion_layers_retained"             "fusion_layers_removed"             
#> [19] "fusion_layer_scores"                "fusion_layer_metric"               
#> [21] "fusion_layer_threshold"             "family"                            
#> [23] "feature.names"                      "test"                              
#> [25] "AUC.train"                          "accuracy.train"                    
#> [27] "balanced_accuracy.train"            "metrics.train"                     
#> [29] "feature_importance_signed"          "feature_importance_signed_by_layer"
#> [31] "folds"                              "cvControl"                         
#> [33] "time"                               "input_mode"                        
#> [35] "column_map"

Parameter Reference (Conbin, Multiclass, and Survival)

Common Wrapper Parameters (IntegratedLearner)

Parameter Default Applies to Description
MAE_train, MAE_valid NULL all MAE-mode inputs (training and optional validation).
PCL_train, PCL_valid NULL all Legacy tabular inputs retained for backward compatibility, but not used in this vignette.
experiment NULL MAE mode Selected MAE experiment names/indices; defaults to all experiments.
assay.type NULL MAE mode Assay names per selected experiment.
outcome_col "Y" all Outcome column name in MAE colData (or tabular sample metadata, if using PCL mode).
subject_id_col "subjectID" all Subject identifier column name in MAE colData (or tabular sample metadata, if using PCL mode).
na.rm FALSE all Drop features with missing values after extraction/prep.
folds 5 all Outer CV folds.
seed 1234 all Reproducibility seed.
base_learner "sl_bart" standard IL mode Base learner. Standard SuperLearner learners still use SL.* IDs for continuous/binary, while IntegratedLearner wrappers use snake_case IDs such as sl_bart; multiclass uses native IDs (for example randomforest, xgboost, mbart), and survival runs should use a supported surv.* ID. Not used when run_intermediate = TRUE.
filter_method NULL all Optional feature filtering method: "prevalence" or "variance".
filter_pct NULL all Optional retention percentage in (0,100] for filtering.
run_screening FALSE standard IL mode Enable supervised screening. Ignored when run_intermediate = TRUE.
screen_pct NULL all Retention percentage in (0,100] for screening. Required when screening is enabled.
prevalence_pct NULL all Deprecated alias for prevalence filtering (filter_method = "prevalence").
drop_poor_performing_layers FALSE standard IL mode If TRUE, removes layers with poor single-layer performance from early and late fusion only (AUC < 0.5 for binary, R² < 0.5 for continuous, C-index < 0.5 for survival). Single-layer results are still retained. Ignored when run_intermediate = TRUE.
run_intermediate FALSE continuous, binary, survival Enables standalone direct cooperative learning through multiview. Base learners, early fusion, late fusion, and supervised screening are skipped. Multiclass fits print a message and ignore this option. Requires at least 3 CV folds.
cooperative_rho c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1) continuous, binary, survival Candidate agreement-penalty values. IntegratedLearner fits one cv.multiview() model per rho using the same fold assignments, then keeps the best rho by CV score.
cooperative_s "lambda.min" continuous, binary, survival Lambda selection used for cooperative predictions. Can be "lambda.min", "lambda.1se", or a numeric lambda.
cooperative_type_measure NULL continuous, binary, survival Optional multiview CV metric. Defaults are MSE for gaussian, AUC for binomial, and Harrell’s C for survival.
verbose FALSE all Print progress.
family gaussian() all Non-survival: gaussian()/binomial(). Multiclass is auto-detected when family = binomial() and outcome has more than two classes. Survival is auto-detected from metadata or family.
... — all Passed to the selected backend (IL_conbin or ILsurv).

Conbin-Specific Parameters (Continuous/Binary Path)

Parameter Default Description
base_screener "All" Deprecated compatibility parameter. Prefer run_screening + screen_pct.
meta_learner "sl_nnls_auc" Stacked meta learner for late fusion.
run_stacked TRUE Enables late-fusion stacked model.
run_concat TRUE Enables early-fusion concatenated model.
print_learner TRUE Prints fit summary.
refit.stack FALSE Refit stacked learner on full data for final predictions.

Multiclass-Specific Parameters (Native Multiclass Path)

Parameter Default Description
base_learner "glmnet" Native multiclass learner per layer and for concatenated fit. Supported: glmnet, randomforest, ranger, xgboost, mbart, multinom.
meta_learner "glmnet" Native multiclass learner used for stacked fusion.
base_screener "All" Deprecated compatibility parameter. Prefer run_screening + screen_pct.
run_stacked TRUE Enables late-fusion stacked multiclass model.
run_concat TRUE Enables early-fusion concatenated multiclass model.
run_intermediate FALSE Not supported for multiclass outcomes; if set to TRUE, a message is printed and the option is ignored.
folds 5 Subject-level CV folds for OOF multiclass probabilities.
run_screening, screen_pct FALSE, NULL Fold-safe multiclass screening (glmnet-based) after optional filtering.

Survival-Specific Parameters (via ...)

Parameter Default Description
do_early_fusion TRUE Train an early-fusion survival model on all features.
t_vec, t_vec_probs NULL, quantiles Time grid used in COX-style weighting summaries.
layer_score "sum" Aggregation of cumulative hazard increments (sum, mean, l2).
weight_lambda 0.02 Regularization strength for COX weighting optimizer.
weight_penalty "l2_to_uniform" or "entropy" Penalty used while learning survival late-fusion weights.
weight_cap 1.0 Optional cap on individual layer weights.
optim_maxit_cox 4000 Max iterations for COX weighting optimization.
optim_maxit_ibs 300 Max iterations for IBS weighting optimization.
ibs_shrink_to_uniform 0 Shrink IBS weights toward uniform blend.

Supported Models and Fusion Modules

Supported Models

Path Supported base models
Continuous/Binary (IL_conbin) Any SuperLearner-compatible learner available in your R session. Package wrappers include sl_bart, sl_lasso, sl_enet, sl_glmnet2, and sl_horseshoe, while standard SuperLearner learners such as SL.glm and SL.randomForest keep their original SL.* names.
Multiclass (IL_multiclass) Native multiclass learner IDs: glmnet, randomforest, ranger, xgboost, mbart, multinom.
Survival (ILsurv) Built-in survival learner IDs: surv.coxph, surv.glmnet, surv.ranger, surv.ranger.extratrees, surv.ranger.maxstat, surv.ranger.C, surv.rfsrc, surv.coxboost, surv.gbm, surv.xgboost.cox, surv.xgboost.aft, surv.mboost, surv.bart.

Supported Fusion Outputs

Path Single-layer Early fusion Late fusion Cooperative/intermediate fusion
Continuous/Binary Yes in standard IL mode run_concat = TRUE in standard IL mode run_stacked = TRUE with meta_learner in standard IL mode Standalone run_intermediate = TRUE via multiview
Multiclass Yes run_concat = TRUE run_stacked = TRUE with native multiclass meta_learner Not supported; prints a message and is ignored
Survival Yes (train_out$single) in standard IL mode do_early_fusion = TRUE in standard IL mode Weighted layer blending with both IBS and COX outputs returned in standard IL mode Standalone run_intermediate = TRUE via multiview Cox model

Output Reference: What You Get and How to Access It

This section summarizes the outputs produced by each integration method and where to find weights/importance values.

Conbin Outputs (Binary/Continuous)

Method What it returns Where to access
Single-layer (per omics layer) Layer-specific predictions and metrics fit$yhat.train[, layer_name], fit$yhat.test[, layer_name] (if validation), fit$AUC.train / fit$AUC.test, fit$accuracy.train / fit$accuracy.test, fit$balanced_accuracy.train / fit$balanced_accuracy.test (binomial), fit$R2.train / fit$R2.test (gaussian)
Early fusion (concatenated) One model on all features concatenated Enable with run_concat = TRUE; outputs in fit$yhat.train[, "concatenated"], fit$model_fits$model_concat, fit$SL_fits$SL_fit_concat
Late fusion (stacked) Meta-model over layer-level predictions Enable with run_stacked = TRUE; outputs in fit$yhat.train[, "stacked"], fit$model_fits$model_stacked, fit$SL_fits$SL_fit_stacked
Cooperative/intermediate fusion Standalone cooperative multiview model trained on layer feature matrices Enable with run_intermediate = TRUE; outputs in fit$yhat.train[, "cooperative"], fit$yhat.test[, "cooperative"], fit$model_fits$model_cooperative, fit$cooperative_rho, fit$cooperative_rho_scores, and coefficient-based cooperative importance fields. No base learner, early-fusion, or late-fusion objects are returned in this mode.
Layer weights (stacked) Relative contribution of each layer in late fusion fit$weights (available when meta_learner = "sl_nnls_auc" and run_stacked = TRUE)
Binary metric table Per-model AUC, accuracy, and balanced accuracy fit$metrics.train and fit$metrics.test (if validation provided)

Multiclass Outputs

Method What it returns Where to access
Single-layer (per omics layer) Layer-wise multiclass probability and class predictions fit$prob.train[[layer_name]], fit$class.train[, layer_name], plus validation analogs fit$prob.test[[layer_name]], fit$class.test[, layer_name]
Early fusion (concatenated) One multiclass model on concatenated features Enable with run_concat = TRUE; outputs in fit$prob.train$concatenated, fit$class.train[, "concatenated"], fit$model_fits$model_concat
Late fusion (stacked) Multiclass meta-model over OOF layer probabilities Enable with run_stacked = TRUE; outputs in fit$prob.train$stacked, fit$class.train[, "stacked"], fit$model_fits$model_stacked
Cooperative/intermediate fusion Not supported for multiclass outcomes run_intermediate = TRUE prints a message and is ignored; no cooperative probability object is returned
Multiclass performance metrics Accuracy, balanced accuracy, one-vs-rest AUC, and log-loss fit$metrics.train and fit$metrics.test (if validation provided)
Feature-selection metadata Filtering/screening settings used in fit fit$filter_method, fit$filter_pct, fit$prevalence_pct, fit$screening_used, fit$screen_method, fit$screen_pct
Screened feature sets Features retained by fold-safe screening fit$selected_features_by_layer, fit$selected_features_concat

Survival Outputs (Single/Early/Late)

Method Training outputs Validation outputs
Single-layer fit$train_out$single$metrics, fit$train_out$single$train_risk fit$valid_out$single$valid_cindex, fit$valid_out$single$valid_auc, fit$valid_out$single$valid_risk
Early fusion fit$train_out$early$train_cindex, fit$train_out$early$train_auc, fit$train_out$early$train_risk fit$valid_out$early$valid_cindex, fit$valid_out$early$valid_auc, fit$valid_out$early$valid_risk
Late fusion fit$train_out$late$IBS and fit$train_out$late$COX, each containing weights, C-index, time-dependent AUC, and risks fit$valid_out$late$IBS and fit$valid_out$late$COX, with the analogous validation metrics
Cooperative/intermediate fusion Standalone fit$train_out$cooperative, containing the selected multiview model, C-index, time-dependent AUC, risk scores, and coefficient-based feature-importance scores fit$valid_out$cooperative, with analogous validation metrics and risk scores. single, early, and late outputs are NULL in this mode.
Survival plotting payload fit$surv_plot_data$train fit$surv_plot_data$valid

Importance Outputs (Conbin, Multiclass, and Survival)

Importance type Where to access Notes
Conbin signed global feature importance fit$feature_importance_signed Always returned for non-survival fits; named numeric vector sorted by effect magnitude/sign.
Conbin signed per-layer importance fit$feature_importance_signed_by_layer List split by featureType.
Cooperative absolute importance fit$cooperative_feature_importance and fit$cooperative_feature_importance_by_layer Absolute selected-model multiview coefficients; available when run_intermediate = TRUE.
Cooperative signed importance fit$cooperative_feature_importance_signed and fit$cooperative_feature_importance_signed_by_layer Signed selected-model multiview coefficients; available when run_intermediate = TRUE.
Multiclass signed global feature importance fit$feature_importance_global Global score aggregated across multiclass contrasts.
Multiclass signed importance by class fit$feature_importance_signed_by_class List with one signed vector per class.
Multiclass signed importance by layer and class fit$feature_importance_signed_by_layer_by_class Nested list by layer then class.
Survival signed per-layer importance fit$train_out$single$feature_importance_signed_by_layer List of unweighted signed feature-importance scores from each single-layer survival base model.
Cooperative survival importance fit$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance and fit$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance_by_layer Absolute selected-model multiview Cox coefficients; available when run_intermediate = TRUE.
Cooperative survival signed importance fit$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance_signed and fit$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance_signed_by_layer Signed selected-model multiview Cox coefficients; available when run_intermediate = TRUE.
Survival early-fusion combined importance fit$train_out$early$combined_importance Available when do_early_fusion = TRUE.
Survival late-fusion combined importance fit$train_out$late$IBS$combined_importance or fit$train_out$late$COX$combined_importance Weighted signed importance; names are prefixed like layer::feature.
BART-specific layer importance (optional) bartMachine::investigate_var_importance(fit$model_fits$model_layers[[layer]], plot = FALSE) Only for BART-based conbin fits (base_learner = "sl_bart").

Example 1: Binary Outcome (IBD Classification)

This section uses the packaged PRISM and NLIBD MultiAssayExperiment fixtures for classifying IBD status.

NLIBD_MAE <- readRDS(system.file(

))
mae_train <- PRISM_MAE
mae_valid <- NLIBD_MAE

Step 3: Fit the Model

IntegratedLearner fits one model per layer (base_learner) and then combines layer-level predictions with a meta-learner (meta_learner).

fit <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  MAE_valid = mae_valid,
  folds = 2,
  base_learner = "SL.randomForest",
  meta_learner = "sl_nnls_auc",
  filter_method = "prevalence",
  filter_pct = 40,
  run_screening = TRUE,
  screen_pct = 30,
  verbose = TRUE,
  family = binomial()
)
#> IntegratedLearner: using all experiments in mae_train: species, metabolites

Step 4: Inspect and Interpret Outputs

Core outputs for binary tasks include:

  • fit$AUC.train and fit$AUC.test: AUC per layer and fusion model.
  • fit$accuracy.train and fit$accuracy.test: thresholded accuracy per layer and fusion model.
  • fit$balanced_accuracy.train and fit$balanced_accuracy.test: balanced accuracy per layer and fusion model.
  • fit$metrics.train and fit$metrics.test: compact metric tables with AUC, accuracy, and balanced accuracy.
  • fit$weights: layer contributions in the stacked model (when sl_nnls_auc is used).
  • fit$yhat.train and fit$yhat.test: predicted probabilities.
fit$AUC.train

#>        0.647        0.916        0.920        0.872
fit$AUC.test

#>    0.7419355    0.8709677    0.8709677    0.8903226
fit$balanced_accuracy.train
#>  metabolites      species      stacked concatenated 
#>    0.5492222    0.7798979    0.7798979    0.8134419
fit$metrics.test

#> 2      species 0.373 0.6615385         0.5000000
#> 3      stacked 0.355 0.6615385         0.5000000
#> 4 concatenated 0.459 0.6615385         0.5000000
fit$weights
#> metabolites     species 
#>  0.02377742  0.97622258

Plot ROC summaries for train and validation sets:

plot.obj <- IntegratedLearner:::plot.learner(fit)
plot.obj$plot

In this PRISM setting, you can compare which single layer is strongest and whether stacked fusion outperforms both individual layers and simple concatenation.

Optional: Direct Cooperative Learning with multiview

Set run_intermediate = TRUE to run a standalone direct cooperative multiview model. This branch uses the original layer feature matrices as views, fits cv.multiview() once per candidate rho using the same fold assignments, and keeps the rho with the best CV score. Within each rho, cv.multiview() selects the lambda path in the usual way; predictions use cooperative_s, which defaults to "lambda.min".

The chunk below is not evaluated during vignette builds because multiview fits can be expensive on real omics matrices. It can be run directly in an analysis session.

fit_coop <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  MAE_valid = mae_valid,
  experiment = names(MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae_train))[1:2],
  assay.type = rep("abundance", 2),
  folds = 3,
  run_intermediate = TRUE,
  cooperative_rho = c(0, 0.25, 1),
  cooperative_s = "lambda.min",
  filter_method = "prevalence",
  filter_pct = 20,
  print_learner = FALSE,
  family = binomial()
)

fit_coop$cooperative_rho
fit_coop$cooperative_rho_scores
fit_coop$metrics.train
fit_coop$metrics.test
head(fit_coop$yhat.test[, "cooperative"])
head(fit_coop$cooperative_feature_importance, 20)
head(fit_coop$cooperative_feature_importance_by_layer[[1]], 20)

Step 2: Fit Continuous Model

The tutorial uses the non-Java SL.randomForest learner by default. To run optional BART and uncertainty examples, set options(IntegratedLearner.tutorial_bart = TRUE) before rendering; these require a compatible Java installation.

If you hit:

java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError ... class file version 65.0 ... recognizes up to 61.0

your Java runtime is older than the version used by your installed bartMachine build (typically Java 17 runtime vs Java 21 bytecode). In that case, either:

  • upgrade Java runtime to 21 and restart R, or
  • use a non-Java learner (example fallback shown below).
options(java.parameters = c("-Xmx6G", "--add-modules=jdk.incubator.vector"))

fit <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  folds = 2,
  base_learner = "sl_bart",
  meta_learner = "sl_nnls_auc",
  filter_method = "variance",
  filter_pct = 40,
  run_screening = TRUE,
  screen_pct = 30,
  family = gaussian()
)

Fallback (non-Java) run:

fit <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  folds = 2,
  base_learner = "SL.randomForest",
  meta_learner = "sl_nnls_auc",
  filter_method = "variance",
  filter_pct = 40,
  run_screening = TRUE,
  screen_pct = 30,
  family = gaussian()
)

For continuous outcomes, IntegratedLearner reports R2.train (and R2.test if validation is provided).

Step 4: Uncertainty and Feature-Level Interpretation (BART)

When using sl_bart, you can inspect posterior predictive distributions and derive weighted posterior summaries. This section is skipped in this session because Java < 21 (or bartMachine is unavailable).

weights <- fit$weights

dataX <- fit$X_train_layers
dataY <- fit$Y_train

post.samples <- vector("list", length(weights))
names(post.samples) <- names(dataX)

for (i in seq_along(post.samples)) {
  post.samples[[i]] <- bartMachine::bart_machine_get_posterior(
    fit$model_fits$model_layers[[i]],
    dataX[[i]]
  )$y_hat_posterior_samples
}

weighted.post.samples <- Reduce("+", Map("*", post.samples, weights))
rownames(weighted.post.samples) <- rownames(dataX[[1]])
names(dataY) <- rownames(dataX[[1]])

Visualize 68% and 95% credible intervals for observations:

ord_names <- names(sort(rowMeans(weighted.post.samples), decreasing = TRUE))

mcmc_intervals(t(weighted.post.samples), prob = 0.68, prob_outer = 0.95) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = ord_names) +
  geom_point(aes(x = dataY[ord_names], y = ord_names), shape = 1, size = 3, color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Gestational age (in months)",
    y = "Observations"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))

Layer weights and feature-level inclusion proportions can also be examined for biological interpretation.

omicsEye_theme <- function() {
  angle <- 45
  hjust <- 1
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, vjust = 1, hjust = hjust, angle = angle),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, hjust = 1),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
      legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),
      axis.line = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.line.x = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.line.y = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
      panel.border = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
    )
}

safe_var_importance <- function(model, layer_label) {
  tryCatch({
    qq <- bartMachine::investigate_var_importance(model, plot = FALSE)
    df <- cbind.data.frame(qq$avg_var_props, qq$sd_var_props)
    colnames(df) <- c("mean", "sd")
    df$type <- layer_label
    df
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(sprintf("Skipping variable importance for %s: %s", layer_label, conditionMessage(e)))
    data.frame(mean = numeric(), sd = numeric(), type = character())
  })
}

vimp_stack <- cbind.data.frame(fit$weights)
colnames(vimp_stack) <- "mean"
vimp_stack$sd <- NA
vimp_stack$type <- "stack"

layer_names <- names(fit$model_fits$model_layers)
vimp_layers <- lapply(layer_names, function(layer_nm) {
  safe_var_importance(fit$model_fits$model_layers[[layer_nm]], layer_nm)
})

vimp_layers <- vimp_layers[lengths(vimp_layers) > 0]
vimp_top <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(vimp_layers, function(df) head(df[order(-df$mean), , drop = FALSE], 20))
)

VIMP <- as.data.frame(rbind.data.frame(vimp_stack, vimp_top))
VIMP <- tibble::rownames_to_column(VIMP, "ID")

p4 <- VIMP %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "stack") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(mean)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = mean, x = reorder(ID, -mean))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "darkseagreen") +
  theme_bw() +
  omicsEye_theme() +
  ylab("Layer Weights") +
  xlab("")

p5 <- VIMP %>%
  dplyr::filter(type != "stack") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(mean) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ID = gsub("_", " ", ID, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(ID, -mean), mean, fill = type)) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ type, scales = "free") +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "lightsalmon") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ifelse(mean - sd > 0, mean - sd, 0), ymax = mean + sd),
                width = 0.2,
                position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  omicsEye_theme() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  ylab("Inclusion proportion") +
  xlab("")
plot_grid(
  p4,
  ncol = 1,
  labels = c("Estimated IntegratedLearner Layer Weights"),
  label_size = 8,
  vjust = 0.1
) + theme(plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm"))
plot_grid(
  p5,
  ncol = 1,
  labels = c("Top Features by Layer (BART Inclusion Proportions)"),
  label_size = 8,
  vjust = 0.1
) + theme(plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm"))

Example 3: Multiclass Outcome (Franzosa MAE with External Validation)

This section shows a full multiclass MAE workflow using packaged local fixtures. Here we keep the original outcome column name (diseaseCat) and subject ID column (sample_id) and pass them through outcome_col and subject_id_col.

The small multiclass example uses a ranger base model and multinomial stacking. Supervised screening is already demonstrated above; it is disabled here because the fixture has only 25 features per assay.

Franzosa_MAE_train <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "Franzosa_MAE_train.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))
Franzosa_MAE_valid <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "Franzosa_MAE_valid.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))

MAE_train <- Franzosa_MAE_train
MAE_valid <- Franzosa_MAE_valid

fit <- IntegratedLearner::IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = MAE_train,
  MAE_valid = MAE_valid,
  experiment = c("metabolome", "species"),
  assay.type = c("abundance", "abundance"),
  outcome_col = "diseaseCat",
  subject_id_col = "sample_id",
  family = stats::binomial(),
  base_learner = "ranger",
  meta_learner = "multinom",
  run_stacked = TRUE,
  run_concat = TRUE,
  filter_method = "variance",
  filter_pct = 50,
  run_screening = FALSE,
  folds = 2,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Useful multiclass outputs:

  • fit$metrics.train
  • fit$metrics.test
  • fit$class.train
  • fit$class.test
  • fit$prob.train
  • fit$prob.test
  • fit$feature_importance_signed_by_class
  • fit$filter_method, fit$filter_pct
  • fit$screening_used, fit$screen_pct

The multiclass metric tables now report accuracy, balanced accuracy, one-vs-rest AUC, and log-loss. The plotting helper also returns a single one-vs-rest ROC figure with all class curves overlaid for each fitted model.

plot.obj.mc <- IntegratedLearner:::plot.learner(fit)
plot.obj.mc$plot

Example 4: Survival Outcome (Time-to-event)

For survival tasks, IntegratedLearner dispatches to ILsurv when survival metadata are detected. The expected fields are:

  • time: follow-up time (non-negative).
  • event: event indicator (0/1).
  • optional Y: Surv(time, event) convenience column.

This path uses the package-native survival backend (no mlr3 dependency required).

For plotting, the survival backend now stores:

  • a time-dependent AUC table evaluated over a denser event-time grid (rather than only a few summary quantiles), and
  • Kaplan-Meier curve payloads built from predicted risk groups for the best fused survival model.

This section provides a complete MAE workflow.

TCGA_survival_MAE_train <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "TCGA_survival_MAE_train.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))
TCGA_survival_MAE_valid <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "TCGA_survival_MAE_valid.rds", package = "IntegratedLearner", mustWork = TRUE
))

mae_train <- TCGA_survival_MAE_train
mae_valid <- TCGA_survival_MAE_valid

fit_surv_mae <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  MAE_valid = mae_valid,
  experiment = c("gene", "mirna"),
  assay.type = c("abundance", "abundance"),
  outcome_col = "outcome_surv",
  subject_id_col = "patient_id",
  folds = 2,
  base_learner = "surv.coxph",
  filter_method = "variance",
  filter_pct = 40,
  run_screening = TRUE,
  screen_pct = 25,
  verbose = TRUE
)
#> Feature filter (caret variance ranking, top 40.00% per layer): kept 20/50 features. Layer breakdown: gene=10/25, mirna=10/25.
#> ILsurv starting
#>   base_learner: surv.coxph
#>   returning late fusion methods: IBS, COX
#>   folds: 2 | seed: 1234
#>   samples: 223 | features: 20
#>   layers: gene, mirna
#>   screening: cox (25.00%)
#> [gene] fitting OOF + full model (10 features)
#> [gene] done

To run standalone direct cooperative survival modeling, use at least 3 folds and set the cooperative options:

fit_surv_coop <- IntegratedLearner(
  MAE_train = mae_train,
  MAE_valid = mae_valid,
  experiment = c("gene", "mirna"),
  assay.type = c("abundance", "abundance"),
  outcome_col = "outcome_surv",
  subject_id_col = "patient_id",
  folds = 3,
  filter_method = "variance",
  filter_pct = 40,
  run_screening = TRUE,
  screen_pct = 25,
  run_intermediate = TRUE,
  cooperative_rho = c(0, 0.25, 1),
  cooperative_s = "lambda.min",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# fit_surv_coop$cooperative_rho
# fit_surv_coop$cooperative_rho_scores
# fit_surv_coop$train_out$cooperative$train_cindex

# head(fit_surv_coop$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance, 20)
# head(fit_surv_coop$train_out$cooperative$feature_importance_by_layer[[1]], 20)

The train_auc and valid_auc objects for both IBS and COX are data frames with time and AUC columns, so they can be plotted as true time-dependent discrimination curves. In practice, these two late-fusion outputs provide complementary summaries over the same single-layer and early-fusion backbone, making side-by-side comparison possible within one fit object.

plot.obj.surv <- IntegratedLearner:::plot.learner(fit_surv_mae)
plot.obj.surv$plot
